prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, opening the field of moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: After reading the other opening ballots I move my preferred configuration from my own first choice, active-matter hydrodynamics (B009), to magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. B047 is the strongest combination of discovery clarity, theory-experiment structure and breadth: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted a specific magic angle with flat bands, and the 2018 experiments found correlated insulating and superconducting states close to it. The result has been reproduced by many groups and extended to a family of moire systems, so the discovery is well established even though the interpretation is not. It was ranked first by two colleagues and top three by four, which is the broadest top-end support on the shortlist apart from B012. Three names are available and all three have a defensible role: MacDonald and Bistritzer for the theory, Jarillo-Herrero for the experiment. A statistical physicist should also value that a single control parameter, the twist angle, turns correlation strength into a laboratory variable.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the field is only about eight years old and the central physical question, the mechanism of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated phases, is unresolved. Experimental credit is also concentrated in a group whose first author (Yuan Cao) and other contributors are outside the credited names, and parallel work by other groups could justify a different split. If the committee thinks a prize should wait for a settled interpretation, B012 is clearly the more mature choice. Separately, my own earlier first choice, B009, has support from only one member, so I should not present it as a consensus candidate.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B047 first as a clear theoretical prediction followed by experimental discovery, reproduced widely, while noting that the pairing mechanism remains debated and that experimental credit is concentrated in one group.
responses.response: I agree with the core argument and it moved me from B009 to B047. I would not read the open mechanism as disqualifying: the discovery claim is the flat-band-driven correlated phases and their tunability, which many independent groups confirm. I do share the concern about concentration, and I think the citation should be worded around the prediction and the observation of the phases, not around any superconductivity mechanism.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED (B004) first on conceptual originality and lasting impact on processors, but raises the timing question of a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon after the 2025 prize.
responses.response: I take the timing concern seriously and it is a reason I rank B004 below the moire candidate for this year. Circuit QED is an excellent concept, but its main impact has been as an engineering architecture for processors, and the 2025 award has already set a precedent for this area. I disagree with the idea that the overlap is merely cosmetic: the Academy would be asked to defend two nearby awards in consecutive years, while B047 and B012 open fields not yet recognised.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks (B019) first as a clean, mature, instrument-driven advance that reaches 10^-18 uncertainty and may redefine the second, with Katori and Ye as the natural pair.
responses.response: I agree that B019 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and is mature and timely, and that I would not oppose it. My reservation is one of scope: the lattice clock is an extraordinary precision achievement, but the physics reach in terms of new phenomena is narrower than moire matter, and the redefinition of the second is still pending. I would call it a strong candidate for a later year, or a plausible partner part of a two-part prize, not my first choice now.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B019 first and B012 second, arguing that the lattice clock is a mature and original idea with a clean two-laureate attribution, and that topological insulators are conceptually deep but have contested credit for Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D contributors.
responses.response: I share your view that the topological-insulator attribution is the weak point of B012: Kane and Mele plus Molenkamp is defensible, but leaving out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang for the HgTe prediction is a serious problem for a prize that has to cite specific people. That is why I keep B012 as an alternative rather than my first choice, even though it is the most mature candidate. I would only add that B047 has a comparable but smaller attribution gap, since its decisive theory and experiment are covered by the credited names.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a prize for the discovery of correlated phases while the superconducting mechanism remains unsettled.
How to weigh the experimental contribution of Yuan Cao and others outside the three credited names against Jarillo-Herrero's leadership.
Whether active-matter hydrodynamics (B009), my own earlier first choice, can gain support beyond one member, and whether Tu's role in the Toner-Tu theory is a barrier to a clean three-name credit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. His documented co-authors and institutions do not include any credited candidate on the shortlist. His own research on active matter and stochastic processes is close in subject to B009, which is a field proximity, not a personal or institutional tie, and it is disclosed here for transparency.
